progress.evidence:
requirement_violation: src/packages/datacenter/facilityScene/dataCenterMaksimReferenceScene.ts:1063–1104 groups mains by individual plantId and emits a separate supply/return pair for each heat-rejection unit, rather than consolidating units into duty-row headers. Its lines 992–1007 also connect otherwise-unused units directly to room loads. The generic path independently groups by plantId at src/packages/datacenter/facilityScene/dataCenterFacilitySceneConnections.ts:1982–2028. This does not implement doc/product-requirements.md:200–206: one pair per duty row per independent train, pairCount = trainMultiplier × ceil(dutyUnitCount / unitsPerHeaderRow), with standby joining its train header. Repository search finds sizeDataCenterCoolingTrunksV1 only at its definition and in coolingTrunkSizing.test.ts, not in production callers. The inspected facility-pipe-60mw-adaptive-3-yard-1440.png and -430.png goldens show numerous parallel cooling runs covering the halls; they do not establish the required row-level consolidation.
requirement_violation: src/packages/datacenter/facilityScene/dataCenterMaksimReferenceScene.ts:1098 sizes a main as min(0.35, max(0.115, 0.06 × sqrt(routes.length))); dataCenterFacilitySceneConnections.ts:2018 uses the same formula with ids.length. Both measure connection count, not served thermal duty or coolant flow, and impose a fixed upper clamp. facilityScene.ts:2264 passes authored.radius directly to the rendered route. This contradicts doc/product-requirements.md:203–207, which requires package-derived flow sizing and radius proportional to sqrt(served duty) at fixed temperature rise and velocity. The duty-based helper at dataCenterFacilityEquipmentSizing.ts:283–295 is tested in isolation but is not called by either production builder.

audit.findings:
Identity: ROOT HEAD=2222fb3f05cef1004739665a588c67d973f9b214, clean tree. The named commit 95f835d3d is not an ancestor of HEAD (merge-base exit 1). Its content reached HEAD as cherry-pick 77d14444d, which has the same title, touches the same one file (dataCenterMaksimReferenceScene.ts, +53/-3) and has a '(cherry picked from 95f835d3d)' trailer. Companion commit 530e9b4d9 reached HEAD as f5824909c.

The model-level oracle passes. src/__tests__/coolingTrunks.test.ts ran 11/11: supply count equals return count, every rejector is connected on both supply and return, footprint crossings are zero, segments are orthogonal, nothing runs outside the shell, and supply and return mains are paired.

The e2e 'AI Project draws paired cooling mains and a see-through buried return in Heat' (product-root.spec.ts:3446) passed at 1440 and 430. report.json stats: expected 2, unexpected 0; exit-code.txt is 0.

The visible requirement is not met. The user asked why everything is only blue when the warm orange pipes should be about as many. In my own HEAD screenshots in Heat, the hall pipework is almost all cold cyan (#28d8ff). Warm return (#ffb347) shows only as small orange stubs and fittings. The buried return draws as faint, barely visible red see-through lines. Pixel count on the hall crop of the 1440 capture (600,420–1100,780, scaled 2x): about 103 warm-orange pixels against about 6053 cyan. On the whole canvas: warm 521 vs cold 1849 at 1440, and warm 111 vs cold 585 at 430. The canvas counts include orange generators and cyan label leader lines.

So warm and cold are equal in the scene data but not in what the user sees. The complaint 'всё только синее' still holds at HEAD in the Facility Heat view: Facility → 3D → Layers → Heat, loaded example configuration.

Side note: dataCenterMaximProjectExample.test.ts has 2 failing tests at HEAD. They cover plan-label anchors and a q-cooling-method completeness gap. Neither is about cooling pipe geometry; I am reporting them, not counting them toward this verdict. The requirement's attached images (#1 and #2) were not available to this audit.
